chase: Wasn't going to chase you. Then you ran past my grate.
Three rooms over, and I can still hear your shoes.
Left at the grate, then down. I know which way you'll go.
I came through the wall so you'd stop going in circles.
I'm not rushing. I'm just never stopping either.
Faster now. You can hear me, which means I'm too close.
Dropping down from the grate now. Don't look up.
Keep running. The metal ticks louder every time you turn.
Your footsteps are on the tile below. Mine are on the metal above.
Two halls, one shaft, and you're trapped between them.
You changed direction. The vent noticed before you did.
I'm closing the distance one grate at a time. Don't stop now.
You can run, but this floor has only so many doors.
You're breathing hard. I can hear it through two walls.
I'm coming through the grate. Keep your head down.
You ran past my grate, so now you're mine.
Three rooms behind you, and gaining slowly.
catch: Got you. Out of the duct and back into the hall.
Got you. Hold still and let me take you back.
Caught at the grate. I didn't even have to climb down.
Caught you on the seam. You shouldn't have stepped there.
Hands where I can see them. The shaft is closed now.
Got you by the sleeve. Don't pull, the sheet metal tears.
Caught. Walk back to the hall with me, nice and slow.
Quietly taken from the grille. Nobody upstairs heard a thing.
Dragged you clear of the grate before anyone else came.
Got one. The others will hear about it at the grate later.
That one was easy. You should have stayed on the tile.
Taken from the ceiling hatch. Quietest thing I've done all day.
Caught on the ladder. Should have looked up before climbing.
You're back in the hall now. Sit down and wait for them.
Got you at the duct mouth. Out you come.
Caught in the vent. Don't kick, it's undignified.
Caught you. Hold still, I'll lower you down.
hear: You'll hear a scrape first. Then I'm already there.
The grille rattles once. That's your warning. Nobody listens to those.
Something knocked two rooms over. I'm going to look.
A door slammed below. I'm moving before it finishes echoing.
That was a shout. I'll take the duct to see who made it.
Glass broke on the ground floor. I'm on my way.
Footsteps on the stairs. Light ones, and careless.
Metal scraping in the room below. That isn't the ventilation.
Something fell off a shelf. I'll check it before the others do.
Somebody's running in the hall. Fast, careless, loud. I'm going.
A thump in the ceiling. I'd say that's a person.
Quiet in the ducts. Quiet is how I get closer.
Listening is the job nobody thanks you for.
I heard a cabinet close. Someone is hiding inside it.
Quiet is good. Quiet means I'm the first to hear trouble.
A scrape in the vent. I'm already moving.
Grille rattled twice. That's you, isn't it?
Something dropped in the duct. Coming down.
search: Lost you at the grate. Don't make me come looking.
You got past me. Fine. Don't tell anyone I said that.
You stop at every door. Doors are how you lose yourself.
Ducts go everywhere. You've only seen the front rooms.
I'm following the draft. You leave a trail of cold air.
No trail here. I'll check the ducts above each room.
You vanished past the grate. Fine. Back to mapping, then.
Lost the sound. I'll wait here and listen again.
Nothing in the east hall. Back to the vents, then.
You slipped out of my reach. I'll circle back through the shaft.
Gone quiet. Quiet doesn't mean gone, I know that much.
I'll go back on patrol. Don't get comfortable, I'll be listening.
Where did you go? Not a single scrape to follow.
No footsteps, no moving air. I'll start the search over.
You keep returning to the same room. Boring for both of us.
stunned: Ow. Who swung a crowbar at the grate?
My head is still ringing from that taser. Give me a second.
That hit nearly took my ear off. Rude.
Stunned. Fine. The vent stays mine, though.
Hold on. My joints are locked up and clicking.
Shaking it off. Give me a moment to find my footing.
The taser fried my hinges for a second. I'll be fine.
Can't feel my left hand. Don't gloat about it.
Stuck in the grate, and it's your fault.
Recovering. Don't come near me until I can see straight.
Three seconds of static, then I'm back in the shaft.
Whatever you hit me with is still humming in my ears.
That was rude. Really rude. I'll remember that.
On the floor now, but the grate is still mine.
Held by the arm. Let go, I'll walk where you want.
hide_spot: Hiding behind the crates. Cute. The air still gives you away.
A locker door with a gap. I can see your shoes from here.
Still hiding? Fine. I'll wait in the vent until you move.
Your breathing carried all the way up the shaft.
I felt you step on the seam. Heavy step, heavy mistake.
Locker, bed, or crate. Each one has a gap I can see.
Quiet in the locker. Shame about the shoes poking out.
Under the bed is the first place I look. Every time.
I'm walking past the crate. Hold your breath, if you like.
Hiding in a cabinet? Clever. Cabinets have grilles too.
Nice spot. Unfortunately it's right under my grate.
I'm opening the wardrobe next. Hope you're comfortable.
Breathe slower, and maybe I'll walk right past you.
The bed creaks when you move. I'm listening for it.
light: Flashlight on. Great. Now the whole duct can see you.
Light up the shaft again and I'll drop straight onto you.
You switched your flashlight off. Smart. Now breathe quieter.
You stood in the light for three seconds. Three. I counted.
Put the flashlight down, or everyone will know where you are.
Flashlight in my face. Lovely. Now I'm squinting like a fool.
That beam hurts. Point it at the floor, please.
You're dazzling me through the grate. Turn that thing away.
I'm dazzled. Give me a second to find you again.
Lamp's too bright in here. Shut it off or I'll find you anyway.
Your light just hit my grille. I see you now, so stay put.
Bright light, bright target. I'd turn it off if I were you.
Every time you flick that beam, the shaft lights up for me.
Stop dazzling me. I'm trying to hear where you are.
idle: I'm not lonely. I just like the walls better than people.
The vents are where I sulk. Nobody bothers you in a shaft.
I'd rather be in a shaft than in a room full of you.
Don't ask about the map. It's half finished and very private.
Sheet metal makes a fine notebook if you press hard enough.
Mapping the ducts again. Nobody asked, and nobody will read it.
Somebody take the front hall. I've got the back ones.
You all keep watching the stairs. Nobody watches the ceiling.
Everyone check the vents before you panic next time.
I scratch my map into the metal. Every duct gets a line.
Don't tell anyone I said that, but you're doing fine.
You lot are loud. Good. I always know where you are.
Nothing to chase right now. Just me and the warm pipes.
Tapping a rhythm on the sheet metal. Don't ask me why.
ability: Every second you spend in the vents, I get a little quicker.
Crawl through the shaft and I speed up. Walk out and I slow down.
Open halls slow me down. The ducts speed me up.
The ducts are the only place I really get to run.
The longer you stay in my ducts, the faster I get.
Nobody sees me in the ducts until they climb in after me.
I'm hidden until somebody enters the shafts. Then I'm not.
Sheet metal is loud, so I keep my weight off the seams.
Four rooms share this shaft. I can come out of any of them.
Out here I'm steady. Inside the shaft, I'm not.
I'm crawling along the sheet metal on all fours.
You stepped into the vents. Now the air belongs to me.
Climbing out right beside you. Surprise, I'm here.
Nothing can see me in the duct. I'm just a draft.
mechanic: Hands off that grate, it's my path and not yours.
If you're going to run, run the long way round.
Down the shaft and out the next grille. Keep moving.
The shaft is open. Your move, and then mine.
Every room in this lounge has a hatch. I know all of them.
Relay on the shelf? Leave it alone, it's on my path.
Battery near the vent hatch. Grab it before I do.
Doors lock behind you, but grates never do.
Crates by the stairs hide a grate. Watch your feet.
Stairs creak and the vents don't. Pick your path wisely.
Sabotage the duct fan and I'll hear it from three floors away.
Don't drop the battery in the shaft. It rolls forever.
A fall through a ceiling tile lands you right in my shaft.
Use the door, not the vent. Unless you want to see me.
Radar pinged the grate. Nice try, but I knew it was there.
The relay is hidden in the vent. Look up.
Batteries rest on the grate ledge. Grab them.
Keep off the grates or they clatter loudly.
